title: Automate Monthly Report Scraping
preferred_referent: 📍 External monthly Texas reporting automation specification
boundary: Automate monthly reporting by combining Excel-entered production data with scraped Texas Comptroller values, applying a fixed-percentage tax-credit rule, exporting required PDF forms, and exporting production columns for a SQLite-based QuickDecline workflow.
acceptance: Working Excel-based automation, reproducible report-population logic, scraper behavior for monthly tax-deduction values, SQLite export, client-maintainable documentation, and walkthrough support.
result: PROTOTYPE PASS — official Texas source targets were mapped; a synthetic District 5/6 Excel pipeline, configurable credit arithmetic, two-column SQLite export, schedule parser fixture, and automated parser/SQLite tests were built. Filing-ready PDF/schema mapping remains client-dependent.
next_movement: Obtain the client spreadsheet, exact fixed-credit rule, fillable PDF templates/field IDs, and QuickDecline SQLite schema; then replace prototype mappings, run a live Comptroller fetch, populate the real forms, and validate report totals before any filing use.
blockers: Client monthly spreadsheet/template is not public.
Exact client fixed-credit rule is not public.
Fillable PDF field identifiers are not mapped.
QuickDecline schema and exact two export columns are not public.
Live government-page scraper should be revalidated against the current page before production use.
resume_bullets: Mapped official Texas Comptroller and Railroad Commission reporting sources and built a bounded monthly-production automation prototype spanning Excel, web-schedule parsing, configurable credit arithmetic, and SQLite export.
Built and passed fixture tests for Comptroller schedule parsing, credit arithmetic, and a two-column QuickDecline-style SQLite handoff while explicitly isolating filing-ready client dependencies.
notes: Official source map includes Comptroller low-producing gas credit schedule, natural-gas forms, and RRC Form PR source.
Prototype is explicitly not filing-ready and does not infer the client tax rule from public eligibility data.
